To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the premise that impact monitoring is impossible is correct, but that it can be accomplished if the other time series needed to define the impact is generated by process-based models.

the best approach to impact detection is to use process-based simulation models to generate predictions of environmental conditions in the absence of the proposed impact and then to compare these predictions with actual measurements of environmental conditions after the impact.

• Environmental impact assessment (EIA) is an exercise in uncertainty analysis, • Impact assessment is an iterative process of prediction and comparison, • Monitoring can be used to check predictions, and • Monitoring can be most effective when used to check predictions made with the aid of process-based simulation models
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a better understanding of the role of environmental monitoring in environmental impact analysis.
the development of a methodology for the design of environmental monitoring programs to detect the effects of environmental change.
the development of a methodology for assessing the ecological effects of a proposed development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, strictly speaking impact monitoring is not possible.
the best use of impact monitoring in EIA is to reduce uncertainty in the prediction of impact by providing data for model validation.
the best monitoring approach is the use of simulation models to generate the control time series, and that this approach should be applied in the majority of situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best approach for monitoring environmental impacts in the future is the use of process models to predict what the impacts should be, followed by monitoring to detect whether or not the predicted impacts actually occur.
monitoring can only be used to reduce uncertainty in impact predictions.
the most important contribution of environmental monitoring to impact analysis is not in the detection of impacts, but in reducing uncertainty about the impacts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monitoring in environmental-impact assessment should be seen as a tool to reduce uncertainty in predictions of impact.

monitoring can only be used to reduce the uncertainty associated with predictions of impacts, and that the best use of monitoring data is to improve the performance of process-based simulation models.
, while impact monitoring is impossible in principle, it can be useful in practice.
